solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Processing for labs to do in criminal evidence

indicators.note: material that is processed is worked over and changed, so the three words before the last are rearranged

explanation.surface: Forensic scientists are asked to process something found at a crime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Processing' sounds like lab work; it is the anagram signal on LABS TO DO, giving BLOODSTA, with IN kept as it is. 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of spilt blood at a scene is a classic piece of proof used against a suspect.

clue.text: Second son in delightful Cambridge area

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back or support it

explanation.surface: A second son lives in a pleasant part of Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Backs are the riverside lawns behind several Cambridge colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: The college grounds along the Cam are a famous, picturesque stretch of the university town.

clue.text: Complete dismissals!

definitions.meaning: two batsmen given out one after the other in cricket

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman dismissed is out, so two dismissals are one out and then another.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated phrase means utter or thorough, and read literally it is two cricket dismissals.

clue.text: Disheartened on demo with hunt sabotaged

indicators.note: a sabotaged thing is wrecked and disrupted, so the four preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Protesters are dejected after hunt saboteurs ruined their march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sabotaged' fits the hunt-protest picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a downcast face, so it means dejected or unhappy.

clue.text: Worker sent up takes in dress for Hindu empress

indicators.note: takes in means the reversed worker swallows the next piece
in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
a sari is the garment worn by Hindu women

explanation.surface: A labourer is mocked for wearing an Indian garment for a Hindu ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hindu empress' tempts RANI; the empress is Russian, and 'dress for Hindu' gives SARI inside TNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a Russian tsar or a female ruler in her own right.

clue.text: Current MP and others seek cash fund

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A sitting politician and colleagues look for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present'; it is I, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: An imprest is an advance of money held for small expenses, like petty cash.

clue.text: Constant smoker worried about gas inhaled

indicators.note: something inhaled is taken inside, so the gas symbol goes into the middle
about means turned round, so the word for worried is read backwards

parts.note: to worry at something is to gnaw or eat at it, so worried means ate
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: A chain smoker gets anxious about the fumes they breathe in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ATE into ETA, and 'inhaled' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is almost always emitting a plume, so it is jokingly a perpetual puffer.

clue.text: One opposed to other manual workers is Hitch

definitions.text: One opposed to other manual workers
definitions.meaning: the digit that is opposable to the fingers of the hand
to hitch a ride by holding out a hand at the roadside

explanation.surface: One worker opposes their colleagues, which is a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manual workers' are fingers, workers of the hand, not labourers.
explanation.definitionFit: The short digit opposes the fingers, and it is also the verb for hitchhiking.

clue.text: He was great unknown in a famous rowing club

indicators.note: in means the unknown letter goes inside the club's name

parts.note: Leander Club is a famous rowing club at Henley-on-Thames
X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A great man, anonymous, belonged to a well-known rowing club.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander Club, at Henley-on-Thames, England, is one of the world's oldest rowing clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Macedonian king Alexander the Great conquered most of the known world.

clue.text: Sad Tyre languishes — that's talk around another port

indicators.note: sad here means in a sorry state, so the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The ancient port of Tyre is in decline, and people discuss a different harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad' is the anagram signal on TYRE LANGUISHES. 'another port' because Tyre is a port too: the Thames estuary, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is given to the accent spoken in the Thames estuary area east of London.

clue.text: Native American in California cheers midlands side

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
WBA is West Bromwich Albion, a football club from the English Midlands

explanation.surface: An American Indian in California applauds an English football team from the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' here is a sports team: West Bromwich Albion, a club from the English Midlands, abbreviated WBA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catawba are a tribe of the Carolinas; the name is also a native American grape variety.

clue.text: Put up with northern runner's attitude

parts.note: to post a notice is to put it up
the Ure is a river (a runner) in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a northern athlete's arrogant manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is the crossword word for a river; the Ure flows through North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Posture can mean the stance or position someone takes on an issue, as well as bodily bearing.

clue.text: Controversial karate instructor against entering competition

parts.note: sensi is a spelling of sensei, a martial arts teacher, listed in Collins

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the letter for against goes inside the word for competition

parts.note: a tie is a cup match, a competition
V stands for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A disputed martial arts teacher objects to joining a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: The instructor is spelt SENSI here, a Collins variant of the more usual SENSEI.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensitive topic is a touchy, delicate one likely to provoke dispute.

clue.text: Classy business graduate keeps rupees in dark place

parts.note: U means upper class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the rupee letter sits within the degree

parts.note: MBA is a Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: An upmarket MBA holder hoards Indian currency somewhere shady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' for upper class is a crossword convention from the U and non-U language debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the fully shadowed region cast by an object, as in an eclipse.

clue.text: Doctor Who's end — it's due

indicators.note: the end of the word Who means only its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A fan says the finale of the TV series Doctor Who is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Who' looks like the TV show; it splits into DR and the last letter of 'Who'.
explanation.definitionFit: A droit is a right or a legal entitlement, something owed to someone.

clue.text: Bound to have whipped cream that fills now

indicators.note: fills means the beaten letters go inside the word for now

parts.note: date as in up to date means now, the present

indicators.note: whipped cream is beaten, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to have whipped cream as a filling right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whipped' rearranges CREAM to EMARC, which 'fills' DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound an area is to mark its limits, to fix its borders.

clue.text: End matter in pursuit of wife or daughter

parts.note: to be after someone is to be chasing them

explanation.surface: A man chasing either his wife or his daughter says it is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: An afterword is a closing section of a book, material printed at the back.

clue.text: Preventing single to leg after Oval cricketer saves six?

indicators.note: after places the single and leg pieces behind the rest

parts.note: O is an oval shape

indicators.note: saves means keeps safe inside, so the numeral goes within

parts.note: a bat is a batsman
VI is six in Roman numerals
I is one, single
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: A batsman at the Oval, a London cricket ground, scores a single to leg and stops a six.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oval' suggests the London ground but just gives its shape. 'saves' puts the numeral inside the cricketer; 'after' sets the single and the leg side at the end. 'leg' is the cricket on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Obviation is the act of forestalling something, heading it off in advance.

clue.text: Decrepit mummy runs away to an Egyptian deity

indicators.note: runs away says the letter for runs leaves the word for mummy

parts.note: mummy is a familiar word for one's mother
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Aten was the sun disc god of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: An Egyptian mummy, rotting, flees towards a god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' suggests Egypt but means mother here; 'runs away' removes R from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chewed by insects is shabby and worn out, hence old and decrepit.

clue.text: Cat in river gets fish

indicators.note: in means the cat word goes inside the river

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire
Leo is the lion, a big cat

explanation.surface: A cat in a river catches a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a Hampshire river in southern England, famous for trout.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleost is any bony fish, the main group of ray-finned species.

clue.text: Grandma quick to produce cloth

parts.note: nan is a British word for a grandmother
keen means sharp or quick, as of mind

explanation.surface: A granny is eager to make fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton fabric first made in Nanjing.

clue.text: Young swimmer always around lake

indicators.note: around means the word for always surrounds the lake letter

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful

explanation.surface: A young competitive swimmer forever training around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a baby eel, a juvenile fish migrating upriver.

clue.text: Money one may charge unwary tourist?

definitions.meaning: a large horned animal on safari that might rush at a careless visitor

explanation.surface: A fee a scammer might extract from an unsuspecting visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like billing a tourist; in the second sense it means a beast stampeding at one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is archaic slang for cash and also short for a thick-skinned African beast that charges.

clue.text: Film director beginning to go red

indicators.note: beginning to go means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Michael Winner was the director of Death Wish

explanation.surface: A film director starts blushing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' is a ring on an archery target, the one just outside the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target, the ring next to the bull is called this and is usually coloured red.

clue.text: Sovereign prince and King George in Bath

indicators.note: in means the following pieces sit inside the word for bath

parts.note: lave is an old word for wash or bathe
taken as written
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A ruling prince and King George are spotted in the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' looks like the English spa city; it is LAVE, an old word for washing.
explanation.definitionFit: A landgrave was a German count with sovereign authority over his territory.

clue.text: Man reversed into drive-in restaurant

indicators.note: reversed means the concealed letters read backwards
into means the letters lie within the run of words

explanation.surface: A man backs his car into a drive-in diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed into' looks like a car crash; the man's name lies backwards in 'drivE IN REstaurant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie is a common male given name, so a man.

clue.text: Girl lacking restraint pulled over tree

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name

indicators.note: pulled over means turned back, so the letters for lacking restraint are reversed

parts.note: OTT is over the top, excessive

explanation.surface: A reckless girl driver is stopped by police by a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled over' looks like a police stop, but it is the reversal signal. OTT means over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Annatto is a small tropical American tree whose seeds give an orange dye.

clue.text: Something impressed in unled rebellion

indicators.note: unled means without its leader, so the first letter of the word for rebellion goes

parts.note: sedition is incitement to rebellion

explanation.surface: Something made a mark during a leaderless uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressed' is the printing sense: an edition is pressed onto paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An edition is a print run, the copies stamped out by a press at one time.

clue.text: Neighbouring country causes English exasperation

parts.note: ire means anger or exasperation

explanation.surface: A country next door that infuriates the English.
explanation.walkthrough: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland, Britain's neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland lies next to Britain, the setter's home, so it is the adjacent nation.

clue.text: Gets excited about unique layer round ancient site

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go outside the next pieces
excited letters are stirred up, so the word Gets is rearranged

parts.note: one means single, unique
a hen is a bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up over a unique hen walking around a historic monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' shuffles Gets, and 'about' wraps the result round the next two pieces. 'layer' is the bird that lays eggs; 'round' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wiltshire monument is a prehistoric circle of standing stones, so it is a circular old site.
